findings: START CONTENTION: pgrep -c headless_shell = 18, loadavg 8.05 -- at/above the cap of 8. Authoring phase first, no browser.

SURVEY 1 - THE WHOLE HOSTILE POPULATION OF THE PROVINCE IS TWO ROWS. game/data/world/encounters.json has exactly 2 encounters: dres-raid-party (4 inf_trash + 2 inf_trash net-throwers, absent_when_flag the_sixty_are_protected) and deep-kin-war-brood (3 inf_trash). Nine bodies, all the SAME statblock, and neither has an (x,z). The encounter records carry `regions: [...]` as a LABEL only -- nothing places them.

SURVEY 2 - WHERE PLACEMENT ACTUALLY HAPPENS: engine.js:761 `for (const e of patch.encounters || []) this.spawnEncounter(e.id, e.x, e.z, e)` inside applyNamedState. So a hostile exists ONLY if a hand-written state file names it with coordinates. Same shape of defect the giver agent found for NPCs: a hand-placed scene is exactly as populated as somebody remembered to type.

SURVEY 3 - THE STREAM PUMP IS THE RIGHT CONSUMER SLOT. Engine._streamProvince() runs from Engine._afterStep(), which the province-stream builder proved covers EVERY way the world advances (stepFrames, the rAF accumulator, walkRoute/walkPath/travelRide). That is where a population that follows the player belongs.

SURVEY 4 - RESPAWN IS ALREADY BUILT AND DATA-DRIVEN and must not be broken: game/data/world/respawn.json + game/src/sim/death.js, with engine._classifyOnSpawn() supplying named/unique/boss/merchant/trainer/questActor from three writers (statblock, world map fog gates, spawn opts). sim.npcs is a separate array no respawn path iterates.

SURVEY 5 - souls are on the statblocks already (W1-SOULS): inf_trash 136, drowned_lesser 50, beast_slitherfang 72, cst_sap_speaker 137, guard_legion 176, drowned_greater 334, champion_hist_marked 2423, 15 props 0. 7 fightable statblocks is the whole roster.

SURVEY 6 - THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE KILLED EVERY STEPPING PROBE: character/encounter.js openingFor() THROWS for an encounter that declares neither race_behaviour nor behaviour_rule='hostile_below_disposition', and stepEncounters() calls it once per encounter member PER FRAME. A wilderness roster added without a third rule would take down the fixed step for the whole project the moment the player walked near one -- the same shape as W1-02's unlisted event name. Added `always_hostile` additively; the two existing rules are byte-unchanged.

SURVEY 7 - USABLE ROSTER IS FIVE STATBLOCKS, not seven. champion_hist_marked and cst_sap_speaker are the two FOG-GATE BOSSES (game/data/world/hearths.json fog_gates) and are both in respawn.json never_respawn_ids. Placing either in the wilderness would put a permanently-dead 2,423-soul body on a road. Wilderness templates use inf_trash(136), drowned_lesser(50), drowned_greater(334), guard_legion(176), beast_slitherfang(72) only.

SURVEY 8 - NO RANGED/DUELIST/TURTLE/AMBUSHER/ordinary-CASTER STATBLOCK EXISTS, so RI-AI05 §D's per-region archetype MIX is unreachable on this roster and no template fakes one. Declared in encounters.json absent_roles_declared rather than hidden.

SURVEY 9 - THE GEOMETRY IS ALL THERE: roads.json 10 legs / 25,056.9 m trunk / point polylines every ~12 m; regions.json 13 regions with danger_tier 1-5 and bounds; pois.json 42 (8 settlement, 16 minor-settlement, 10 landmark, 8 waystation); hearths.json 29 hearths (13 of them `critical-path` along the crossing) + 2 fog gates. The crossing is named_routes.crossing: legs stormhold-helstrom + helstrom-blackrose + blackrose-lilmoth, 6,816 m, 56.8 walk-min.

DENSITY CONTRACT, reconciled from two items that agree: RI-AI07 §D encounters per TM 0.88 (0.59-1.29), enemies per TM 1.65 (1.05-2.45), enemies per encounter 1.9 (1.4-2.6), solo:grouped 55:45; RI-WLD02 D9 hostile groups per minute of wilderness road walking 0.7-1.2 (fail <0.4 or >2.0). A TM is 120 m at S17's 2.0 m/s, so both are the SAME density and 0.88/TM = one encounter per 136 m.
ARITHMETIC THAT SETS THE GROUPED SIZES: 0.55x1 + 0.45xG = 1.9 => G = 3.0. Grouped encounters must average exactly 3 bodies for the mean to land on RI-AI07's 1.9 at the declared 55:45 split.

GENERATED PLACEMENT, first full build: 144 posts / 267 bodies / 34,646 souls. Wilderness road density 0.884 encounters per traversal minute against RI-AI07 §D's target of 0.88 and band 0.59-1.29, and inside RI-WLD02 D9's 0.7-1.2. Enemies per TM 1.598 (target 1.65, band 1.05-2.45). Enemies per encounter 1.854 (target 1.9, band 1.4-2.6). Solo:grouped 59:41 (band 45:55-65:35). Grouped mean bodies 2.968 against the derivation's required 3.0. 17 gank-duo posts.

THE CROSSING, generated: 27 posts, 38 bodies, 4,554 souls over 6,825 m / 56.9 walk-minutes, crossing salt-hills(t3), valus-ridge(t4), stone-forest(t3), deep-marshes(t5), blackwood(t2), western-rootlands(t1). Fully cleared it pays LEVEL 8 on RI-PRG01's shipped curve. Before this the same walk passed six sentries worth 816 souls = level 2.

FIRST GENERATOR RUN WAS WRONG AND THE MISTAKE IS WORTH KEEPING: at hearth clear 45 m + ramp 150 m, the THIRTEEN critical-path hearths strung along the crossing suppressed 390 m of every 500 m of it and the road came out at 0.431 enc/TM against a floor of 0.59. A HEARTH IS A CHECKPOINT, NOT A SAFE ZONE -- in Souls an enemy stands twenty metres from the bonfire in sight of it. Apron is now 22 m with a 40 m ramp; settlements keep 70+150.

SECOND GENERATOR FIX: a candidate rejected for water/fog-corridor/separation used to consume its unit of density, so a causeway silently cost the road its budget (243 water rejections on the trunk). Rejections now put the unit back, capped at 1.5 so a long causeway does not pile up on the first dry land the far side. 0.541 -> 0.884 enc/TM.

THE INTRODUCTION RULE HAS TO BE A POST-PASS, NOT INLINE. Run along the road in leg order it introduced inf_trash in a TIER-4 region, because that is simply where the crossing's first leg starts. RI-AI05 §D is about what the PLAYER meets first, so the pass now runs over the finished placement ordered by (danger_tier, distance from nearest safety). Resulting order: drowned_lesser, beast_slitherfang, inf_trash (all western-rootlands t1), then guard_legion (stone-forest t3), then drowned_greater (clay-moor t4) -- each solo.

SPAWN COLLISION FOUND BY READING, BEFORE IT COULD FIRE: Engine.spawnEncounter names bodies `${encounterId}-${role}-${i}` and Engine.spawn THROWS on a duplicate eid. Two posts of the same template resident at once would have crashed the fixed step the first time a road carried two marsh sentries. Fixed with an additive opts.tag (the post id); every existing caller passes none and is byte-identical.

THE PROVINCE-CELL GATE IS NOT OPTIONAL: PopulationSystem.step() returns early unless engine.cellFor(sim.env) === 'province'. Without it wilderness bodies would appear in arena_flat and contaminate every combat probe in the project.

S5 HAS A HALF THAT LIVES OUTSIDE sim.entities. DeathSystem.respawnOrdinary() revives ordinary hostiles that are still ENTITIES -- i.e. within ~260 m. RI-PRG04 §1 says every non-unique hostile returns INCLUDING ONES KILLED HOURS AGO, and a post cleared two kilometres back is not in that array. Coupled with a COUNTER (death.ordinaryRespawnEpoch), deliberately not a callback, so respawnOrdinary still touches only sim.entities and the combat bodies and the seam stays structural.

SUCCESSOR-2, CONSUMPTION TOOL WRITTEN: tools/world/population-consumption.mjs, 8 arms A1..A8 (walk / still control / ablation / runtime-radius perturbation / MODEL regenerate+reboot / behaviour / composition via absent_when_flag / S5 respawn). Every arm carries a control that must go the other way.

SMOKE RUN, 600 m of the crossing at 0b2d6ef (pgrep 12, loadavg 5.39 - counts only, no timings claimed): 2/2. Posts materialised at m=119, 269, 419(x2), 599 -- FIVE posts, SIX bodies, ZERO at metre zero, one released behind the player. The world builds its population under a walking player and not at load.
THE ROAD FIGHTS BACK NOW, and this is the number: the census walker lost 335 HP over 630 m WITHOUT EVER ATTACKING (620 -> 285). Before this piece the same 630 m was unopposed.

INSTRUMENT BUG FOUND AND FIXED BY READING THE SMOKE OUTPUT: the walker's HP top-up wrote sim.player.hp, which sim/combat-bridge.js#mirror OVERWRITES from combat.player every step -- so it reported 5 successful top-ups against a walker that was still bleeding out. combat.player is the authority. Anything in this project that heals or reads player HP through sim.player alone is writing to a mirror.

walkRoute() returns `path_m`, NOT `dist_m`. A probe that reads dist_m gets undefined, `undefined < metres` is false, and the walk loop exits after ONE chunk while reporting success. Cost nothing here because it was caught before the first run; it is exactly the shape of a probe that cannot fail.

handle.h() calls die() on an in-page throw and takes the WHOLE PROCESS with it -- right for a verb the tool depends on, fatal for killEntity on a body already down or restAt on a missing hearth. Added a tryH() that goes through page.evaluate and returns {ok,error}.

OWNERSHIP SEAM, read from docs/PLAN.md §3: `combat.encounter.placement` and `combat.encounter.grouping` are W1-12's (enemy AI) declared paths; `world.density.handplacement` is W1-27's and is judged by RI-AI07/RI-WLD01/RI-WLD02/RI-PRG04/RI-WLD09. This piece builds the placement MODEL and its runtime consumer and hands both to those owners; it does not claim their paths, and its numbers are stated against RI-AI07 §D and RI-WLD02 D9 so they can be re-derived.

THE HAND-PLACEMENT RULE DOES NOT FORBID THIS, and I checked rather than assumed. RI-PRG08 §S12's "hand-placed, no procedural generation" is about upgrade MATERIALS. RI-WLD02 §1's POI definition explicitly EXCLUDES "respawning ordinary enemies with no loot" from being POIs at all. Generated posts carry no loot, no material and no drop field (verified over all 144).

LANDMINE IN THE GENERATED DATA, found by auditing my own predecessor's output against RI-WLD02 §1: 22 of the 144 posts carry a field literally named `poi` (the landmark a garrison rings). RI-WLD02 §1 says "a critic finding scatter props tagged `poi` fails the piece outright", and a POI census that counts `poi` keys across world data would count 22 respawning-enemy posts as POIs. Nothing in game/src reads the field. Renaming it to `rings_poi` -- reference, not tag.
